worked_solution:
We note that $m=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

The equation has the denominators $m,\,6m,$ and $12m.$ So first, we find the least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$) of the denominators. We find that

$$
\text{LCM}(m,6m,12m)=12m.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $12m,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{m}+\frac{4+m}{6m} & =\frac{5}{12m} \\ 12m(\frac{3}{m}+\frac{4+m}{6m}) & =12m(\frac{5}{12m}) \\ 12m\cdot \frac{3}{m}+12m\cdot \frac{4+m}{6m} & =12m\cdot \frac{5}{12m} \\ 12\cdot m\cdot \frac{3}{m}+2\cdot 6m\cdot \frac{4+m}{6m} & =12m\cdot \frac{5}{12m} \\ 12\cdot \cancel{m}\cdot \frac{3}{\cancel{m}}+2\cdot \cancel{6m}\cdot \frac{4+m}{\cancel{6m}} & =\cancel{12m}\cdot \frac{5}{\cancel{12m}} \\ 36+2(4+m) & =5\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $m,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}36+2(4+m) & =5 \\ 36+8+2m & =5 \\ 44+2m & =5 \\ 2m & =-39 \\ m & =-\frac{39}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $m=0$ as a solution. However, since $m=-\frac{39}{2}\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $m=-\frac{39}{2}.$
